questions.q: What is the key difference between a GitHub Actions secret and a variable?
options: A secret is encrypted and write-only after saving; a variable is plain text, visible to anyone with repo access
A secret can only be used in one workflow; a variable can be used anywhere
There is no difference — the terms are interchangeable
Variables are always secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN specifically
questions.explain: Secrets are encrypted and can't be viewed again once saved, making them appropriate for sensitive values; variables are plain text, meant for non-sensitive configuration.

questions.q: Where in GitHub does a repository's Actions secrets and variables actually live?
options: Repository Settings, under Secrets and variables → Actions
Directly inside the .github/workflows/ci.yml file
In the repository's README
In the Pull Requests tab
questions.explain: Secrets and variables are configured in the repository's Settings, never written directly into a workflow file.

questions.q: How does a workflow step reference a secret named DOCKERHUB_TOKEN?
options: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_TOKEN }}
${{ vars.DOCKERHUB_TOKEN }}
$DOCKERHUB_TOKEN written as plain YAML text
By pasting its value directly into the workflow file
questions.explain: The secrets context, written as ${{ secrets.NAME }}, resolves a secret's value at run time without ever exposing it in the file.

options: An automatic, run-scoped secret GitHub generates for every workflow run
A secret you must create manually in every repository
A variable used only for setting the AWS region
A token that must be requested from GitHub support
questions.explain: GITHUB_TOKEN is generated automatically for each run and scoped to that run, commonly used to authenticate actions/checkout against the repository.

questions.q: Why is secret masking in logs described as 'not a guarantee'?
options: A step that transforms or splits a secret's value before printing it can still leak it, even though GitHub masks the exact value
Masking only works for variables, never for secrets
Masking is a paid feature not available on all repositories
GitHub never actually masks any values in logs
questions.explain: GitHub masks a secret's literal value wherever it appears, but a step that echoes a transformed or partial version of it can bypass that protection.
